editorial:
Chatroom pulls you into a world where a few lonely teens meet a charming stranger online, only to discover that his friendly words hide something dangerous. You follow Jim, Eva, Emily, and Mo as William wins their trust with quick jokes and bold confidence, making the chatroom feel like a safe place. The movie keeps a tense, uneasy mood because you can sense William is always steering people toward darker choices. It is less about big action and more about how easily trust can be twisted when everyone is hiding behind a screen.

The performances help sell the tension, especially the way William shifts from charming to cold without warning. The pacing stays tight, though some scenes feel a little heavy-handed and the teen drama can get melodramatic. If you enjoy psychological thrillers about online danger, manipulation, and fragile friendships, this one is worth a look. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or pick up the 4K Blu-ray for your collection.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, William's manipulation is exposed as he pushes Jim toward suicide. When they finally meet in person, William tries to convince Jim to jump from a rooftop, but Jim refuses and chooses to live. William, unable to control the situation anymore, falls to his death. Jim survives and gets help, showing that William's power only worked while people stayed trapped in his online world.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological thrillers about online manipulation and teen drama.
